subject: wedding DJs
demo_screen_concept: The Cuebook workspace for the Hart & Moreno reception (Sat, Nov 7, Larkspur Barn). A left sidebar of pages (Run of Show, Requests & Bans, Vendor Contacts, Uncle Protocol). The main pane is the 'Requests & Bans' database with Table / Board / Run of Show view tabs, status filter chips (Queued, Banned, Played anyway, Mom override), live search, a request-count property that increments, and a '+ New request' row. Clicking a row opens a side peek with properties, the guest who asked, and a comment thread. An 'AI summary' button collapses the request inbox into one line. The Run of Show view has a Cha Cha Slide block with a lock toggle that refuses to unlock.
one_liner: A shared workspace for the happiest day of someone else’s life.
brand_voice_notes: Calm operational confidence about a room that has requested Mr. Brightside nine times. Treat family politics as database permissions. No wink or generic startup hype.

hero.h1: Every request. A matter of record.
hero.sub: The shared workspace for wedding DJs. Plan the night, document the bans, and give the mother of the bride her own permission level.

features.title: A paper trail for the dance floor.
features.blurb: Every request gets a status, a witness, and a place in the database. “I already asked the other DJ” is now a queryable claim.

features.title: Family politics, with permissions.
features.blurb: The couple can ban a song. Mum can override the ban. You can record that you advised against it. Everyone has a role.

features.title: A schedule with one exception.
features.blurb: Build a precise run of show around speeches, cake, and the first dance. The Cha Cha Slide has already reserved its slot.

pricing_tiers.name: Dynasty
pricing_tiers.tagline: For families with a procurement team.
perks: A quarterly review with the couple

testimonials.quote: She said she never approved Cotton Eye Joe. I opened the record. We are no longer speaking, but the record is clear.

testimonials.title: Wedding DJ, 46 five-star reviews and one pending dispute

testimonials.quote: I gave the bride’s mother an account. She changed six things before breakfast. Having it in one place has been useful.
testimonials.name: Priya Shah
testimonials.title: Planner, legally distinct from the venue coordinator

testimonials.quote: I tried to remove the Cha Cha Slide. Cuebook declined. It understands the industry.
testimonials.name: Dennis Vale
testimonials.title: Mobile DJ, carries a spare cable for the spare cable

design_direction.style: Modern event-stationery SaaS: cool periwinkle surfaces, navy serif display, spacious centered hero and a wide operational workspace. White event folios provide hierarchy without decorative paper effects.
design_direction.archetype: Product-led workspace landing with a large database preview, unified feature columns, portrait-led testimony and three pricing plans.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Short 180ms color and sheet transitions after user actions. No idle animation. Reduced motion disables transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Centered two-line serif headline above a wide event-workspace preview. Generous blue margins frame the white database. A small event folio and request-status rows make the brief recognizable. Lower sections left aligned.
design_direction.plan_review: Rejected the search default of romantic script fonts and dark audio colors. The DJ sells operational control to wedding clients; cool blue event stationery and a readable database represent that tension. Unique style/palette/font tuple against all seven supplied concepts.

images.rationale: Assets reused for a controlled comparison, not generated by Codex. Typographic hero and document-shaped demo need no photos. The three supplied portraits appear in testimonials. No generation prompts, generation counts, or vision-review verdicts are recorded.
